full_caption: Jasper Jarrowmere, Appellant, v. Two Rivers Realty Trust, Appellee
court: Brightwater Land and Property Court, Grayrock Division
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: Appellant Jasper Jarrowmere is the record owner of the residential building located at 3125 Wicklow Lane, Grayrock, BW, a 8-unit structure operated as rental housing since 1988. Appellee Two Rivers Realty Trust occupied Unit 4C under a written lease dated June 28, 2020.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: The security deposit of $2,100 was not returned within 60 days of surrender, nor was an itemized statement of deductions furnished. The statutory consequence is forfeiture of the landlord's right to retain any portion of the deposit.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: The lease provided for monthly rent of $3,125, due on the first day of each month, with a late charge of $125 assessed on any installment remaining unpaid after the 3th day of the month. The trial court found that this charge operated as a penalty rather than as liquidated damages.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: A tenant electing to withhold rent under the repair-and-deduct statute must (1) give written notice of the defect, (2) allow a reasonable time for cure, and (3) deposit the withheld sums with the clerk of court or into a segregated account. Two Rivers Realty Trust satisfied the first two requirements but did not deposit the withheld rent.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: The record establishes that Jasper Jarrowmere received written notice of the heating defect on April 26, 2026 and did not dispatch a repair contractor until December 7, 2023, an interval of 30 days. During that interval overnight interior temperatures fell below fifty-five degrees on at least eleven occasions.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: The trial court awarded Two Rivers Realty Trust attorney's fees of $22,500 under the reciprocal-fee provision. Where a lease grants fees to the landlord, this State reads the provision as mutual, and the prevailing tenant recovers on the same terms.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: A late fee is enforceable only where it bears a reasonable relationship to the administrative cost actually incurred by the landlord in processing a delinquent payment. A charge of $125 against a monthly obligation of $3,125 exceeds that relationship and is unenforceable to the extent it exceeds five percent of the installment.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: Two Rivers Realty Trust withheld rent for the months of June and September of 2002, asserting that the premises were untenantable by reason of a persistent failure of the heating system and recurring water intrusion at the north wall of the unit.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: Jasper Jarrowmere served a notice to quit on August 18, 2019. The notice recited the ground of non-payment but omitted the amount claimed to be due. A notice to quit that fails to state the sum demanded does not commence the statutory cure period.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: The implied warranty of habitability is not waivable by lease term. Any provision purporting to require a tenant to accept the premises 'as is' is void as against the public policy of this State insofar as it reaches conditions materially affecting health and safety.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: Retaliatory eviction is presumed where a landlord commences a summary possession action within 6 months after a tenant has reported a code violation to the municipal housing inspector. The presumption is rebuttable by clear and convincing evidence of an independent, non-retaliatory ground.

sections.heading: Paragraph 12
sections.text: We affirm in part and reverse in part. The judgment of possession is vacated; the money judgment is remanded for recalculation consistent with the late-fee holding set out above.

sections.heading: RIDER A — LATE CHARGES AND RETURNED PAYMENTS
sections.text: Tenant shall pay a late charge equal to five percent (5%) of the monthly installment for any rent not received by Landlord on or before the 3th day of the month in which it is due. The late charge is agreed to represent Landlord's administrative cost of processing a delinquent payment and is not a penalty or a charge for the use of money. A returned-payment fee of $125 shall be assessed for any instrument returned unpaid. No late charge shall be assessed on a late charge, and no default interest shall accrue on any installment for which a late charge has been assessed.

sections.heading: RIDER B — HABITABILITY, REPAIRS AND ACCESS
sections.text: Landlord shall maintain the heating, plumbing, electrical and structural elements of the Premises in good and safe working order. Tenant shall give Landlord written notice of any condition requiring repair. Landlord shall commence a repair affecting heat, hot water, or sanitation within twenty-four (24) hours of notice and all other repairs within 30 days. If Landlord fails to commence within those periods, Tenant may, after a second written notice, cause the repair to be made and deduct the reasonable cost, not exceeding one month's rent in any twelve-month period, from the next installment. Nothing in this Rider waives the implied warranty of habitability.

sections.heading: RIDER E — SUBLETTING AND EARLY TERMINATION
sections.text: Tenant may not sublet the Premises or assign this Lease without Landlord's written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed. Tenant may terminate early upon 30 days' written notice and payment of a termination fee equal to two (2) monthly installments, provided that no termination fee shall be charged where the termination follows Landlord's material breach, a lawful lease-break for domestic violence, or military relocation orders.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Dispute Resolution
sections.text: Before filing suit, a party shall give written notice of the dispute and the parties shall confer in good faith for not fewer than 3 days, and shall thereafter submit the dispute to non-binding mediation before a mediator experienced in real property matters. This clause does not bar an action for injunctive relief to prevent irreparable harm or an action to preserve the status quo.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Attorney's Fees
sections.text: In any action to enforce or construe this instrument, the prevailing party shall recover its reasonable attorney's fees, expert fees and costs, at trial and on appeal. Where the instrument grants fees to one party only, this clause shall be read as reciprocal and shall entitle the other party to fees on the same terms if that party prevails.
